audit.why: 50.39% over 1661 games with a Skill/Skill/K'Sante/K'Sante/Skill/Skill/Rumble chart matches the kit maths: K'Sante's edge is levels 3-5 when Path Maker is online and Rumble has no item yet, and Rumble's edge is two items and teamfights via The Equalizer's 1750 range. diff EVEN at 6/10 is right. Left as is.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-3 spike was described as 'chain Q-Q-Q into a wall knockup'. K'Sante's Ntofo Strikes reaches its shockwave at 2 stacks, not 3, and that shockwave PULLS enemies in — it is not a knockup and not a wall interaction. The knockback-and-stun is Path Maker (W), which is also what arrives at level 3.
audit.why: Riot text, Ntofo Strikes: 'At 2 stacks, K'Sante fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in.' Path Maker: 'K'Sante charges up, taking reduced damage, then dashes, knocking back and stunning enemies.' The wall interaction belongs to All Out: 'knocks an enemy back, launching them through any wall in their path.'
audit.corrected: Level-3 spike is now Path Maker (14/13/12/11/10s); the wall is attributed to All Out at 6; the pull is attributed to 2 Ntofo Strikes stacks.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three decisive interactions were absent or wrong. (a) 'Use W to block your Electro-Harpoon slow' — Path Maker is damage reduction during a charge, not a projectile block; K'Sante has no blocksProjectiles in his kit, so the harpoons land and the MR shred applies. (b) All Out explicitly costs him defences AND removes Path Maker's knockback and stun — the ulting K'Sante literally cannot lock you down, and this was never stated. (c) Electro Harpoon reduces Magic Resist, so both charges belong before Flamespitter, not after; nothing in either layer said so.
audit.why: Riot text — Path Maker: 'charges up, taking reduced damage, then dashes'. All Out: 'gaining increased damage, healing, and transformed abilities at the cost of reduced defenses' plus Path Maker 'When All Out ... no longer knocks back or stuns'. Electro Harpoon: 'reducing their Magic Resist'.
audit.corrected: Reframed Path Maker as a damage-reduction charge you wait out with Flamespitter (not something that eats your harpoons), stated that All Out trades his stun and his resistances away, and put both harpoons before the cone throughout.

audit.whatIsWrong: The itemization line mentioned anti-heal generically ('his healing fights your pattern') without naming when it matters.
audit.why: K'Sante's only healing in the kit is All Out. Grievous Wounds applied after he ults is wasted; the Oblivion Orb timing is before his two-item window.
audit.corrected: Tied Grievous Wounds explicitly to All Out and to the two-item timing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers credited Rumble's Flamespitter with 'percent-HP' damage ('your percent-HP Q ticks punish every melee step').
audit.why: Riot's Flamespitter text is flat magic damage in a cone for 3 seconds. Rumble's kit file carries no percentHealth flag. The percent-HP burn in this matchup comes from Liandry's Torment, not from the ability.
audit.corrected: Attributed percent-HP burn to Liandry's Torment and left Flamespitter described as what it is.

audit.why: Nothing in the local kit data (ddragon 16.15.1, patch 26.15 live) indicates a recent swing in this pairing, and I did not verify patch history off-line. No patch claim written.

edits.before: K'Sante's levels 1 and 2 are surprisingly manageable — he has no hard lockdown yet and his damage is front-loaded onto three Q charges that telegraph clearly. Use Flamespitter freely on his approach and ride the Danger Zone window; his base stats are tanky but your percent-HP Q ticks punish every melee step. The danger starts at level 3 when he can chain all three Q charges into a wall stun: keep that wall at your back or position away from the lane wall entirely, and never let him pin you. Your W shield absorbs the knockup damage if you time it right, but the silence window that follows is the kill window — stay healthy above 70% and respect his burst pattern rather than trading even at this stage.
edits.after: K'Sante's levels 1 and 2 are manageable — he has no lockdown yet and Ntofo Strikes is a 450-range line on a flat 3.5-second cooldown, so it telegraphs. Walk Flamespitter onto his approach and ride the Danger Zone window; he is tanky, but every melee step he takes costs him. The danger starts at 3 with Path Maker: he charges up taking reduced damage, then dashes out knocking you back and stunning you. That charge is the tell — it is not a projectile block, so your Electro Harpoons still land and still shred his MR, but a Flamespitter poured into it is wasted. Hold the cone until the dash resolves. Two Ntofo Strikes stacks fire a shockwave that pulls you in, so never stand in that line twice, and keep Scrap Shield for the stun rather than the poke.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are K'Sante's clearest edge in this matchup — his tankiness and W-block let him absorb your Flamespitter rotations far better than most melee opponents, and if he lands a wall knockup he can extend into a sustained trade that your Overheat silence only worsens. Freeze near your tower if you are behind, and only short-trade with Q-into-double-E if you have full Heat control and his Q is on cooldown. At 6 the lane shifts: Equalizer does not win the 1v1 against K'Sante directly, but it means you can abandon the losing duel and instead drop the wall on him plus the approaching jungler, turning his all-in into a death. Use Equalizer to punish his teamfighting roams and deny him the coordinated engage his kit is designed around.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are K'Sante's clearest edge. Path Maker's charge soaks a whole Flamespitter rotation at reduced damage and returns every 12-13 seconds, and Footwork adds a shield and a dash every 9. Freeze near your tower if you are behind, and short-trade only when Path Maker is down: both Electro Harpoons first for the magic-resist shred, then the cone. At 6 the lane changes shape rather than tilting. All Out knocks you back through any wall and then dashes onto you, so stop hugging the lane wall — that wall is his tool, not yours. But All Out is bought with his own defences and it removes Path Maker's knockback and stun entirely, so the K'Sante chasing you cannot lock you down. Lay The Equalizer across his path and walk out of the fight he wanted.

edits.before: Two items on K'Sante is the danger window: All Out strips his resistances and turns him into a true duelist with percent-HP damage, W-block to negate your Electro-Harpoon slow, and the raw ability to kill you in the isolation he creates with his R. Never fight him alone in the late game — his kit is built for exactly the 1v1 your kit cannot cleanly resolve. Your win condition is Equalizer on every objective fight: drop the burning wall across the choke before his team can engage, let your frontline collapse the enemies caught inside, and let K'Sante waste All Out on a target your team collapses. You out-scale him in teamfight value, not in side-lane power.
edits.after: Two items on K'Sante is the danger window: All Out gives him healing and a duelist statline, and he manufactures the isolation his kit wants by knocking you through a wall with R. Grievous Wounds has to be on him before he ults, never after — Oblivion Orb is the item that decides those extended fights. Do not duel him alone late; his kit is built for exactly the 1v1 yours cannot resolve. Your win condition is The Equalizer on every objective fight: 1750 range and 80 seconds at rank 3, laid across the choke before his team engages, so his frontline arrives already slowed and burning. You out-scale him in teamfight value, not in side-lane power.

notes: Kit-file flag misfires I deliberately did NOT write into the page: (1) K'Sante's Path Maker carries a "trueDamage" flag and _missing-interactions.json turns that into "K'Sante bypasses stacking resistances (Path Maker)". Riot's description contains no true-damage clause — the flag looks like it parsed "taking reduced damage". Not asserted. (2) K'Sante's Dauntless Instinct carries an "autoReset" flag and _missing-interactions.json calls it an auto-attack reset. Riot's description says his abilities MARK targets to take more damage on his next attack — a damage amp, not a reset. I wrote the mark behaviour implicitly (his ability is the tell) and did not claim a reset. (3) Rumble's Scrap Shield "knockup"/"terrain" flags and The Equalizer's "terrain" flag are misfires; nothing here claims Rumble displaces or creates collision. The biggest genuine error fixed: both layers said K'Sante chains "Q-Q-Q into a wall knockup" and that his W "blocks your Electro-Harpoon slow". Ntofo Strikes shockwaves at 2 stacks and PULLS; the knockback-and-stun is Path Maker; the through-a-wall knockback is All Out; and Path Maker is damage reduction, not a projectile block, so the harpoons and their MR shred always land. Also removed the fabrication that Rumble's Flamespitter deals percent-HP damage — that comes from Liandry's Torment.
